headline: Bruins get steamrolled by Montreal as winning streak hits a dead end
morning_brew: I am not gonna sugarcoat it, that was a damn disaster at the Garden last night. The Canadiens walked in and took it to us, snapping our seven-game home winning streak like it was a cheap pencil. Losing to Montreal is always a kick in the teeth, but watching them score five on us and leapfrog us in the standings makes it sting that much more. It was a pissah of a night, and I spent the third period staring at the ceiling, wondering how a team that was rolling so hard could look that completely lost in their own building.

Jeremy Swayman didn't have his usual stuff, getting chased after giving up four goals, and the defense looked like they were skating through wet concrete for most of the first forty minutes. We finally showed a pulse with Casey Mittelstadt netting a pair, but by then the hole was already deep enough to bury my cousin Jimmy's hopes and dreams. You can't start a rivalry game against the Habs that flat and expect to come away with two points, especially when the other team is playing with that kind of urgency. It was a brutal wake-up call for a team that looked invincible on home ice until the puck dropped.

Now we have to regroup with Minnesota coming into town on Saturday night. I expect a much better effort from the boys because losing two in a row to a team like that is not an option we can afford. I will be back in my usual spot, hoping the defensive breakdowns stay in the past and we start playing the kind of hockey that actually keeps the Duck Boat fund moving in the right direction. It is a long season, but nights like this remind you that nothing in this league comes easy.

news_digest.headline: Canadiens snap Bruins' seven-game winning streak on home ice with 5-2 win
news_digest.dans_take: Getting beat by Montreal is bad enough, but blowing a seven-game streak to them is just insulting to my blood pressure.
